senses.definition: something or someone that one vehemently dislikes
senses.example: Raising taxes was anathema to the party.

senses.definition: to waste away, especially as a result of lack of use
senses.example: Without exercise, the muscles in his leg atrophied.

senses.definition: the gradual decline of effectiveness or vigor due to underuse or neglect
senses.example: The atrophy of local newspapers left many towns without coverage.

senses.definition: to make something greater by adding to it; to increase
senses.example: She took a second job to augment her income.

senses.definition: relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life
senses.example: The painting shows a bucolic scene of cows by a stream.

senses.definition: distress or embarrassment at having failed or been humiliated
senses.example: Much to his chagrin, he forgot his lines on opening night.

senses.definition: a feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad
senses.example: He felt no compunction about lying to the press.

senses.definition: (of a person) pleasant because of a personality, qualities or interests that are similar to one's own
senses.example: She found her new colleagues congenial.

senses.definition: (of a thing) pleasant or agreeable because suited to one's taste or inclination
senses.example: The quiet village was a congenial place to write.

senses.definition: an expert judge in matters of taste
senses.example: A connoisseur of cheese, he could name any variety by its smell.

senses.definition: to violate the prohibition or order of a law, treaty or code of conduct
senses.example: The factory's waste contravened environmental rules.

senses.definition: not openly acknowledged or displayed
senses.example: The agency ran covert operations abroad.

senses.definition: no longer existing or functioning
senses.example: The building once housed a defunct newspaper.

senses.definition: to express disapproval of
senses.example: The author deprecates the habit of judging books by their covers.

senses.definition: to play down; to belittle
senses.example: She tends to deprecate her own achievements.

senses.definition: famous and respected within a particular sphere
senses.example: An eminent surgeon led the inquiry.

words.note: Eminent means distinguished; imminent means about to happen.

senses.definition: soon passing out of sight, memory or existence; quickly fading or disappearing
senses.example: The evanescent glow of the sunset lasted only minutes.

senses.definition: making great demands on one's skill, attention or other resources
senses.example: The work is exacting and requires great patience.

senses.definition: to make an action or process happen sooner or be accomplished more quickly
senses.example: Paying the extra fee will expedite your application.

senses.definition: producing or capable of producing an abundance of offspring or new growth; fertile
senses.example: The fecund soil of the delta feeds millions.

senses.definition: intellectually productive or inventive
senses.example: Her fecund imagination produced a new story every week.

senses.definition: a minor weakness or eccentricity in someone's character
senses.example: We learned to accept each other's foibles.

senses.definition: not having any serious purpose or value
senses.example: The court dismissed the case as frivolous.

senses.definition: (of a person) carefree and not serious
senses.example: His frivolous attitude to money worried his parents.

senses.definition: attempting to avoid notice or attention, typically because of guilt or a belief that discovery would lead to trouble
senses.example: He cast a furtive glance at the exam paper next to him.

senses.definition: a lengthy and aggressive speech
senses.example: The manager delivered a harangue about lateness.

senses.definition: to lecture someone at length in an aggressive and critical manner
senses.example: She harangued the council about the potholes for twenty minutes.

senses.definition: excessive pride or self-confidence
senses.example: In the tragedy, the king's hubris leads to his downfall.

senses.definition: deserving or causing public disgrace or shame
senses.example: The champions suffered an ignominious defeat in the first round.

senses.definition: in accordance with the highest standards; faultless
senses.example: He has impeccable manners.

senses.definition: having little or no money
senses.example: The impecunious student lived on rice and beans.

senses.definition: to formally accuse or charge someone with a serious crime
senses.example: The mayor was indicted for fraud.

senses.definition: impossible to stop or prevent
senses.example: The inexorable rise of sea levels threatens the coast.

senses.definition: a person fighting against a government or invading force; a rebel
senses.example: Insurgents seized control of the northern province.

senses.definition: rising in active revolt
senses.example: The insurgent forces captured the airport.

senses.definition: having or showing a lack of self-control; immoderate
senses.example: The minister apologized for his intemperate remarks.

senses.definition: an unorthodox or independent-minded person
senses.example: A maverick in her party, she often voted with the opposition.

senses.definition: sullen and ill-tempered
senses.example: He became morose after losing his job.

senses.definition: to move or swing back and forth at a regular speed
senses.example: The pendulum oscillated slowly.

senses.definition: to waver between extremes of opinion, action or quality
senses.example: He oscillated between hope and despair.

senses.definition: done or shown openly; plainly apparent
senses.example: There was overt hostility between the two camps.

senses.definition: a typical example or pattern of something; a model
senses.example: The company is a paradigm of good management.

senses.definition: a framework of ideas and assumptions within a field
senses.example: The discovery forced a paradigm shift in physics.

senses.definition: to read something, typically in a thorough or careful way
senses.example: She perused the contract before signing.

words.note: Peruse traditionally means to read carefully, though it is often used to mean skim.

senses.definition: the desire to promote the welfare of others, expressed especially by the generous donation of money to good causes
senses.example: Her philanthropy funded three new hospitals.

senses.definition: (of language or style) concise and forcefully expressive
senses.example: The book is full of pithy advice.

senses.definition: a sign or warning that something, especially something momentous or calamitous, is likely to happen
senses.example: The storm was seen as a portent of disaster.

senses.definition: dangerously high or steep
senses.example: A precipitous path led down to the beach.

senses.definition: (of a change to a worse situation) sudden and dramatic
senses.example: The company's shares suffered a precipitous fall.

senses.definition: (of a person or their behavior) failing to observe the limits of what is permitted or appropriate
senses.example: It would be presumptuous to book the venue before she says yes.

senses.definition: unsophisticated or narrow-minded
senses.example: His provincial attitudes surprised his city friends.

senses.definition: of or concerning a province of a country
senses.example: Provincial elections will be held in May.

senses.definition: an expert in a particular subject or field who is frequently called upon to give opinions about it to the public
senses.example: Political pundits predicted a landslide.

senses.definition: an uneasy feeling of doubt, worry or fear, especially about one's own conduct
senses.example: She had no qualms about asking for a raise.

senses.definition: to sign or give formal consent to a treaty, contract or agreement, making it officially valid
senses.example: Both countries ratified the treaty.

senses.definition: to claim or prove that evidence or an accusation is false
senses.example: The minister rebutted the charges point by point.

senses.definition: unable to keep still or silent and becoming increasingly difficult to control, especially because of impatience or dissatisfaction
senses.example: The crowd grew restive as the delay dragged on.

words.note: Restive means restless or unruly, not restful.

senses.definition: (of a person, especially a man) courteous and refined in manner
senses.example: The urbane diplomat charmed everyone at the dinner.

senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed, frustrated or worried, especially with trivial matters
senses.example: The constant noise vexed the neighbors.

senses.definition: experienced in the imagination through the feelings or actions of another person
senses.example: She took vicarious pleasure in her son's success.

senses.definition: (especially of a woman) attractively lively and animated
senses.example: The vivacious host kept the party going.
